content.title: Thunder vs Suns NBA Playoffs Game 1 highlights: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, OKC rout Phoenix
content.text: Updated April 19, 2026, 7:27 p.m. CTFor Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and the OKC Thunder, it's almost starting to become cliche.Another Bricktown Beatdown in Game 1 of the NBA Playoffs.Last year it was the Memphis Grizzlies getting gored by 51 points in the opener.On Sunday afternoon at Paycom Center, it was the Phoenix Suns' turn in the first round of the Western Conference playoffs.Chalk it up Thunder 119, Suns 84.Gilgeous-Alexander, the reigning NBA MVP, scored 25 points on 5-for-18 shooting.Devin Booker led Phoenix with 23 points on 8-for-17 shooting.Game 2 of the best-of-seven series is set for 8:30 p.m. CT Wednesday.Order new book on Thunder's run to NBA titleThunder vs Suns score updates in Game 1 of NBA Playoffs[ LISTEN UP: Make the "Thunder Buddies" podcast a staple of your starting lineup by following onApple,Spotify andYouTube. ] Thunder vs Suns highlights in Game 1 of 2026 NBA PlayoffsFinal: Thunder 119, Suns 84 | OKC takes Game 1 in NBA PlayoffsShai Gilgeous-Alexander: 25 points, 7 assists and 4 boardsJalen Williams: 22 points, 7 boards and 6 assistsChet Holmgren: 16 points, 7 boards and 2 blocksOKC claims Game 1 of the first-round series. It'll host Game 2 at 8:30 p.m. CT Wednesday.7:34 left in fourth quarter: Thunder 104, Suns 70 | OKC cruising to win in NBA playoff openerJalen Williams sinks the 17-foot jumper, continuing what has been a very impressive performance. He has 22 points, 7 boards and 6 assists in 29 minutes. OKC has a 104-70 lead over Phoenix with 7:34 remaining.End of third quarter: Thunder 97, Suns 66 | Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, OKC rolling in Game 1It's been much of the same in the third frame for the Thunder.Shai Gilgeous-Alexander’s playmaking has been a marvel so far for OKC. He’s up to 25 points, six assists and four rebounds in 29 minutes.The aggression of Dillon Brooks and Devin Booker, who combined to score 11 points during a 10-3 run, helped Phoenix bring the game within 15 points. Booker has 23 points and six rebounds so far for the Suns.But an inevitable response by the Thunder came soon after, sparking a 15-3 run to close the quarter. Brooks and Booker have struggled, combining to shoot 13-of-37 from the field with five turnovers. This one is all but final as OKC is 12 minutes away from being 9-0 in the first round over its last three playoff series’.— Jordan Davis, Staff writerHalftime: Thunder 65, Suns 44 | OKC doesn't let up Talent, size, depth ... all of OKC's advantages were highlighted in the first half. Chet Holmgren starred in the first quarter, but the second quarter was all about Jalen Williams. J-Dub opened the quarter by lobbing an alley-oop to Isaiah Hartenstein. Later, Williams found Cason Wallace on a slick cut. Wallace hung from the rim as Phoenix called another timeout. It's been a little reminiscent of the Thunder's Game 1 against the Grizzlies in the first round last year. OKC beat Memphis by 51 points. This one might not be that bad, but the Thunder is well on its way to another opening playoff game rout. Holmgren leads all scorers with 16 points on 5-of-7 shooting. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander has 13 points, but he's gone just 3-of-10. Jalen Williams has 11 points and six assists. — Joe Mussatto, columnistJaylin Williams exits Thunder-Suns playoff gameThunder center Jaylin Williams exited the game and was taken to the locker room midway through the second quarter Sunday in Game 1 of the NBA Playoffs against the Suns.Williams appeared to have tweaked his ankle after he was whistled for an illegal screen. The Thunder backup center had four rebounds, two points and two assists in six minutes. The Suns are down their starting center in Mark Williams, which still leaves OKC with a big size advantage in Chet Holmgren and Isaiah Hartenstein. —Joe Mussatto, columnist9:05 left in second quarter: Thunder 45, Suns 24 | OKC pours it on PhoenixJalen Williams just found Cason Wallace for an easy dunk, giving him five assists. That also gives OKC a 45-24 lead over Phoenix with 9:05 left in the second quarter.End of the first quarter: Thunder 35, Suns 20 | Phoenix is offensively limited — even more against OKCThe Suns are challenged on the offensive end, ranking as one of the lowest-scoring teams in the NBA this season.Against the Thunder's defense when it's in playoff mode?Yikes.The Suns shot just 33.3% from the floor in the first quarter, hitting just 7 of 21 shots. Other than Devin Booker and Jalen Green, no Phoenix player has hit more than one shot. What's more, the Suns have almost as many turnovers (four) as made shots (seven).They're going to have to figure out how to score more against the Thunder, or the Suns are going to have to clamp down defensively. The Thunder shot 46.2% in the first quarter. That, paired with how OKC held Phoenix defensively, is a good formula for the Thunder.— Jenni Carlson, columnistEnd of the first quarter: Thunder 35, Suns 20 | Chet Holmgren hits 3-pointer at buzzerChet Holmgren: 13 points and 6 reboundsShai Gilgeous-Alexander: 8 points and 3 assistsJalen Williams: 5 points and 2 assists7:04 left in first quarter: Thunder 16, Suns 12 | Dillon Brooks picks up flagrant-1 foul on Chet HolmgrenDillon Brooks has been given a flagrant foul for smacking Chet Holmgren in the face while going for a loose ball. The contact was deemed unnecessary. Thunder starting lineup vs Suns in Game 1 of NBA PlayoffsHere are OKC's Game 1 starters vs. Phoenix:Shai Gilgeous-AlexanderLu DortJalen WilliamsChet HolmgrenIsaiah Hartenstein Suns starting lineup vs Thunder in Game 1 of NBA Playoffs: Mark Williams ruled out for PhoenixHere are Phoenix's Game 1 starters vs. OKC:Devin BookerJalen GreenDillon BrooksJordan GoodwinOso Ighodaro It’s a ‘privilege’ for Thunder to begin playoff run on 31st anniversary of OKC bombingSunday marks the start of the Thunder’s playoff run. The start of its mission to defend its first NBA championship in franchise history, which begins with Game 1 against Phoenix.But it also marks 31 years since the bombing of the Alfred P. Murrah Federal Building in Oklahoma City. A domestic terror attack that took the lives of 168 people and injured hundreds of others.That’s on the minds of OKC’s players, who pride themselves in representing the resiliency of the city every time they step onto the floor. And Sunday will be no different.“I was younger at the time, very young,” Thunder head coach Mark Daigneault said. “But that was, I think, Oklahoma City’s first introduction to the country nationally. It was the first time the city was really on a national stage, and it was obviously a tragic situation where the whole country saw what the city was about. And then a more positive way is that the team has been on a national stage since it’s come here. “The city has been able to represent itself in a more positive way and in a better circumstance. For us to represent the city and honor the victims and the families today with a home playoff game is a privilege for us. We don’t take it lightly. We addressed the team on it yesterday. We’re certainly thinking about all of the families and the victims and the city itself as we take the floor today.”—Justin Martinez, Staff writer What time is Thunder vs Suns game today?Date: Sunday, April 19Time: 2:30 p.m. CTWhere: Paycom Center in Oklahoma CityWatch Thunder vs Suns live on FuboWhat channel is OKC Thunder vs Phoenix Suns on today?TV: ABCHow to watch online: Fubo (free trial)Thunder vs Suns predictions, picksJustin Martinez: OKC 119, Phoenix 106The Thunder is finally at full strength after an injury-filled season, and it should also be rested since most of its rotational players haven't suited up since April 8. I expect OKC to show it's in championship form on Sunday as a result by beating a Phoenix team that simply doesn't have as much talent. The Suns will put up a fight with their physical defense, but Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and company will claim Game 1.Thunder vs Suns betting oddsOdds via BetMGM as of Saturday, April 18Odds: OKC by 14.5Over/under: 215.5Moneyline: OKC -1200 | Phoenix +750Thunder vs Suns injury updatesThunder: Thomas Sorber (right ACL surgical recovery) is out.Suns: Grayson Allen (left hamstring strain) is questionable.
